beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: Dave lays three cards down. "Let's trace how I got to Thursday nights alone with a ledger."

beats.prompt: The past: the read you trusted before you could explain it.
The present: the big push you and your partner pulled off together.
The future: the quiet you needed once the push was over.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Quiz me. If solitude's supposed to be productive, why do I feel worse most Thursdays before I feel better?"

options.text: Feeling worse first just means you're actually looking, not performing calm.
Feeling worse means the Hermit was the wrong read.
You should stop doing this if it feels bad.

elaboration: The Hermit was never about arriving at comfort — the search itself, uneven as it feels, is the actual point of the card.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "So when do I know I've actually found what I was looking for in the numbers?"

options.text: When the small details finally add up into something you can say out loud.
You'll never really know, so stop looking.
The Hermit promises a fixed finish line.

elaboration: The lantern only shows one step at a time — you'll know you've found it when the details finally resolve into a picture you can actually name.

beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: "One thread ties all three: a read you trusted, a push you made together, and the quiet that came after to make sense of both."

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Yeah — I think I finally have the words for what's actually going on in the numbers. Time to actually tell him. Thanks."
